points.description: Names the property: a spanning tree has a single unique path between every pair of nodes (equivalently: it is loop-free yet connects all nodes), so no unnecessary duplicates of packets are sent when broad-/multicasting.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says loop-free or connects all nodes without the unique-path/no-duplicates consequence, or states the property vaguely.

points.description: Modification: multicast group membership information is added to the link state packets, so each node learns which nodes/ISs belong to which multicast groups (a node initially knows only its own groups).
points.partial_credit: Half if only says link state packets are extended or group info is flooded, without clearly linking it to group membership.

points.description: Once topology and group information are distributed to all nodes, each node locally computes the multicast spanning tree from its complete stored state (e.g. with Prim or Kruskal).
points.partial_credit: Half if says nodes compute a tree but not that it is computed locally from the full topology plus group information.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the unique-path/loop-free property with its no-duplicates benefit, plus both parts of the modification: group info added to link state packets, and each node then building the tree locally. Part marks for vague or half-stated ideas, such as only saying "no loops" or "send group info" without more. No marks for a wrong property (e.g. shortest paths or lowest cost) or for describing unmodified link state routing only. Naming Prim or Kruskal is not required.
